worktree_cleanup.title: Working copies on this machine

worktree_cleanup.min_age_description: Days after a copy's last run before it can be cleared. Days, not hours: a run you meant to come back to on Monday should still be there after a holiday.
worktree_cleanup.trunk_description: The branch a copy's work must already be in, whether it was merged or squashed into it. Leave empty to use each repository's own default branch.
worktree_cleanup.summary: {{count}} working copies · {{total}} on disk · {{reclaimable}} would be cleared
worktree_cleanup.advisory: Automatic cleanup is off, so nothing below will be removed. This is what it would do if you switched it on.
worktree_cleanup.empty: No working copies on this machine yet. Parallel mode creates one per task.
worktree_cleanup.reason_removable: Merged, clean and idle — this one would be cleared.
worktree_cleanup.reason_removable_squash: Squashed into trunk, clean and idle — its changes are in the trunk branch even though its commits are not, so this one would be cleared.
worktree_cleanup.reason_uncommitted: Kept: it still has uncommitted changes. Multica never removes a copy holding work that is nowhere else.
worktree_cleanup.reason_unmerged: Kept: its branch is not in the trunk branch yet.
worktree_cleanup.reason_too_recent: Kept: its last run is too recent.
worktree_cleanup.reason_in_use: Kept: a task is running in it right now.
worktree_cleanup.reason_not_ours: Kept: Multica did not create this one, so it is not Multica's to remove.
worktree_cleanup.reason_unknown: Kept: its state could not be read, and unknown is not permission to delete.

migration.title: Migrate across environments (including chats)
migration.description: Pack this workspace's configuration and your chats into a zip.
migration.export_hint: Choose where to save the zip. It includes your chat history — keep it private.

migration.import_hint: Choose a zip, preview the dry run, then apply it to this workspace.
migration.confirm_description: This writes configuration and chats into the current workspace. It cannot be undone from this page.

migration.option_activate_autopilots_hint: Imported automations start triggering as soon as the import finishes. Untick to import them paused.
migration.option_apply_workspace_settings_hint: Context, repositories and attribution settings travel in the bundle and land on this workspace.
migration.option_apply_issue_prefix_hint: Changes the key of every future issue here. Keeps the imported bodies' `DENE-123`-style references pointing at the right issues, so leave it on unless you want this workspace's own prefix. Only applied while this workspace has no issues yet.
migration.autopilots_active: Automations: {{imported}} imported, triggering as soon as the import finishes.
migration.autopilots_activate_hint: Tick “Activate automations after import” and apply to start these straight away.
migration.runtimes_hint: Each imported agent runs on a machine. A single matching runtime is bound automatically; several are yours to pick.
migration.runtime_reason_no_runtime: No runtime on the target instance has provider={{provider}}. Connect this machine's daemon to the target instance (or pick a runtime by hand) and bind again.
migration.runtime_reason_provider_unknown: This bundle carries no source runtime for the agent. Re-export it from the source environment and import again.
migration.option_auto_bind_runtimes_hint: When exactly one target runtime matches the source provider, mode and profile, bind the agent to it. Several candidates are always left for you to pick.
migration.option_include_issues_hint: Export this workspace's tasks, comments, labels and reactions too. The zip grows several times over, and the target workspace has to be empty.
migration.include_issues_requires_empty_target: The task group needs a target workspace that has no tasks at all.
migration.include_issues_empty_target_hint: Create an empty workspace and import into that one. Issue numbers are preserved task by task, so importing into a workspace that already has tasks is refused.
migration.issues_target_not_empty: This workspace already has tasks, so the task group was refused: issue numbers are preserved task by task. Create an empty workspace and import there. On the CLI, `--renumber` shifts the numbers instead — every old number written in a description or comment then points at the wrong task.

routing.title: Routing
routing.description: When an issue is created and whenever its status changes, decide who should be holding it and fill the executor and reviewer slots. Routing never changes status — status is a fact only whoever is doing the work knows.
routing.enabled_description: Switched off, the product behaves exactly as it did before: no routing comments, no mentions. Values already written to issues are kept.
routing.model_description: The model that makes the call. After you save an endpoint and key, available models are loaded automatically; you can still type an id manually.
routing.model_discover_failed: Could not load models. Enter a model id manually.
routing.model_discover_empty: The endpoint returned no models. Enter a model id manually.
routing.threshold_description: Below this the ticket is still dispatched, to the fallback rung (the generic strong seat), and the routing comment says so. Defaults to 0.60.
routing.stale_hours_description: How long a ticket may sit awaiting acceptance with no run working on it before the sweep looks at it. The default action is to put it back in front of the reviewer and change no status; only a pass verdict the reviewer already left on the ticket lets the status be aligned to done. Defaults to 24 hours.
routing.gateway_endpoint_workspace: The model id is sent to this workspace’s own endpoint: {{host}}.
routing.gateway_endpoint_deployment: The model id is sent to the deployment’s shared LLM endpoint: {{host}}.
routing.gateway_protocol_systemone: This endpoint is TypeSafe System One (Jev): routing asks it for a typed judgment with the probabilities behind it, so the confidence it gates on is measured rather than self-reported.
routing.gateway_unset: There is no endpoint to send the model id to — this workspace has not set one, and the deployment has no internal LLM configured (MULTICA_LLM_BASE_URL / MULTICA_LLM_API_KEY). Set an endpoint and key below, or ask whoever runs the server.
routing.gateway_url_description: An OpenAI-compatible base URL, or https://api.typesafe.ai for TypeSafe System One (Jev). Leave both fields empty to use the deployment’s shared endpoint, which is what happens today.
routing.gateway_key_description: Stored encrypted and never shown again — not even masked. Save to replace it; clear to go back to the deployment endpoint.
routing.gateway_key_unstorable: This deployment cannot store a workspace key (neither MULTICA_ROUTING_SECRET_KEY nor JWT_SECRET is set). Only whoever runs the server can fix this.
routing.gateway_pair_incomplete: An endpoint needs both halves. With only one filled in, the deployment’s shared endpoint is used instead.
routing.gateway_default_model: That deployment’s own default model is {{model}}.
routing.filters_placeholder: Supported later; not implemented in this version. Today candidates are narrowed by direction and gated by confidence.
routing.health_never_checked: No call made since the server started

off.detail: While off, everything works exactly as it did before.

incomplete.detail: The switch is on but no model is chosen — this still behaves exactly like off.

enabled.detail: New issues are dispatched automatically, and each decision is explained in a comment on the issue.

ineffective.detail: The model was rejected, is unreachable, was deleted, or is cooling down after repeated failures. Behaves like off; nothing appears on any issue.
